::: {.callout-warning}
## Before you connect anything

**Suspended masses.** Every reference mass in this experiment hangs, or
presses, on the load cell or the beam tip. Never put a hand, a cable or an
instrument underneath a suspended mass, and use a mass hanger or a clamp
rated well above what you load — a mass that slips is a mass in free fall
onto whatever is below it. Load and unload one mass at a time and keep the
load path clear before you touch anything electrical.

**The beam's elastic limit.** The beam is a spring, and springs that are
pushed past their elastic limit do not return: a beam bent into yield stays
bent, and the M1/M2 stiffness relations ([tip deflection and surface
strain](../../hardware/beam-rig.qmd#sec-beam-relations)) become meaningless for it
afterwards, because they assume linear elastic behaviour. Never exceed the
working load $F_\mathrm{work}$ this bench specifies, never add masses faster
than one at a time while watching the reading, and if a reading fails to
return to zero after unloading, stop and inspect the beam before continuing
— see @sec-m1-step-zero.

**The amplifier, before the sensor.** Build and power the instrumentation
amplifier stage first and verify its quiescent output with a DMM, exactly as
[S3 verifies its conditioning stage](../S3-aliasing-filtering/handbook.qmd#sec-s3-step-condition),
before the gauge or the load cell is connected to it. See [Before you connect
anything](../S1-daq-static/handbook.qmd#sec-s1-hardware) in S1 for the pin
tolerance warning, which applies unchanged.
:::

### 1. Identify the board and verify the amplifier {#sec-m1-step-identify}

```bash
arduino-io list
arduino-io info
```

Write down `adc_bits`, `vref_mV` and the `flags` line, as in
[S1](../S1-daq-static/handbook.qmd#sec-s1-step-identify). Then, with the
amplifier built but **no sensor connected**, measure its quiescent (no-input)
output with the DMM and compare it with the design offset from
@eq-m1-required-gain. A discrepancy here is the amplifier's own offset error,
and it is a component of the uncertainty budget in @sec-m1-budget — measure
it before you need it, the same discipline S3 uses for its conditioning
stage.

### 2. Load cell: the loading and unloading sweep {#sec-m1-step-loadcell}

Working from zero to the working load and back, one mass at a time:

```bash
arduino-io mode 15 analog
# masses in increasing order: 0, then each reference mass in turn
arduino-io stream 15 --hz 1000 --seconds 0.2 --csv data/load-loading-000.csv
# ... repeat for each mass, then repeat in decreasing order for unloading
arduino-io stream 15 --hz 1000 --seconds 0.2 --csv data/load-unloading-000.csv
```

::: {.callout-important}
## Load and unload in the same order every time

The hysteresis loop of @eq-m1-hysteresis is only meaningful if the loading
sequence and the unloading sequence visit the *same* nominal forces. Decide
the mass sequence before you start and do not skip a point in either
direction, even if a reading looks unsurprising.
:::

Record each mass's value and its uncertainty (from the balance or the
masses' own calibration) in `channels[].reference_value` and
`.reference_u` — Newtons, from $F = mg$, not kilograms.

### 3. Creep: one mass, held {#sec-m1-step-creep}

Apply a mass at roughly 60–80 % of the load cell's working range and leave it
in place, recording continuously for several minutes:

```bash
arduino-io stream 15 --hz 100 --seconds 60 --csv data/load-creep.csv
```

Do not touch the load, the cell or the bench for the whole hold — vibration
or a bumped table shows up in @eq-m1-creep's residuals as noise, not as
creep, and can hide the effect you are measuring.

### 4. Zero return {#sec-m1-step-zero}

Remove the last mass and record a short zero reading, **without** re-zeroing
or re-taring the instrument:

```bash
arduino-io stream 15 --hz 1000 --seconds 0.2 --csv data/load-zero-return.csv
```

Compare this against the very first zero reading of @sec-m1-step-loadcell.
If the beam or load cell shows a visible permanent set, or the zero has
shifted by more than a few percent of full scale, stop: something in the
loading sequence exceeded its elastic range, and no further reading from this
session should be trusted without re-verifying the mechanics.

### 5. On the beam: quarter, half and full bridge {#sec-m1-step-bridges}

With the strain gauges wired as described in
[bridge sensitivity](handbook.qmd#sec-m1-bridges), apply the same small set
of reference masses at the beam tip for each of the three configurations in
turn:

```bash
arduino-io stream 15 --hz 1000 --seconds 0.2 --csv data/bridge-quarter-000.csv
# ... repeat the quarter-bridge sweep over all reference masses, then
# rewire as a half bridge and repeat at the two endpoint masses, then
# rewire as a full bridge and repeat at the two endpoint masses
```

Use *more* points for the quarter-bridge sweep than for half and full: the
quarter-bridge points are also the load-to-strain calibration
[M2](../M2-hall-displacement/index.qmd) reads back for the stiffness
cross-check, and a sweep needs more than two points to give a fit a residual
at all.

### 6. Temperature compensation {#sec-m1-step-temp}

With the beam **unloaded**, record the quarter bridge and the dummy-gauge
half bridge at the bench's ambient temperature, then change the bench
temperature by a known, moderate amount (a heat gun held at a safe distance,
or a cold pack, whichever your bench provides) and repeat both:

```bash
arduino-io stream 15 --hz 1000 --seconds 0.2 --csv data/temp-quarter-cold.csv
arduino-io stream 15 --hz 1000 --seconds 0.2 --csv data/temp-half-cold.csv
# change the bench temperature, let it stabilize, measure it
arduino-io stream 15 --hz 1000 --seconds 0.2 --csv data/temp-quarter-hot.csv
arduino-io stream 15 --hz 1000 --seconds 0.2 --csv data/temp-half-hot.csv
```

Record the temperature change itself — measured, not assumed — in
`environment.ambient_temperature_C` for each pair and in
`channels[].applied_delta_t_c`, following the extension pattern
[S3 uses](../S3-aliasing-filtering/handbook.qmd#sec-s3-step-sidecar) for its
own generator-frequency and filter fields.

::: {.callout-tip}
## No heat source at the bench yet?

The [reference data](index.qmd#sec-m1-index-data) models the same test
numerically — an apparent strain per kelvin applied directly to each bridge
configuration through the same amplifier and ADC model — so every analysis
task below runs against it unmodified. Repeat with your own runs once a
controlled heat source is available.
:::

### 7. Fill the sidecars {#sec-m1-step-sidecar}

Beyond the fields [S1](../S1-daq-static/handbook.qmd#sec-s1-step-sidecar)
already asks for:

- [ ] `channels[].reference_value` / `.reference_u` — the applied force in
      newtons, from the reference mass and its own uncertainty
- [ ] `channels[].gauge_factor`, `.bridge_excitation_v` — for every
      beam-mounted-gauge run
- [ ] `channels[].bridge_type` — `quarter`, `half` or `full`, for the bridge
      demonstration runs
- [ ] `channels[].applied_delta_t_c` — for the temperature-compensation runs
- [ ] `channels[].load_cell_capacity_n`, `.load_cell_sensitivity_mv_per_v` —
      for the load-cell runs
- [ ] `synthetic: false`
